name: ARC — Anchored Residual Controller: Gârleanu–Pedersen anchor on TASK_915's forecast, IPO-calibrated (closed form), plus a zero-initialised, bounded residual network trained on the book's Sharpe-after-cost
mechanism:
DATA FLOW AND ANCHOR (Stage 0, closed form). Panel = `trader/data.py:137-190` true-UTC daily OHLCV bars, PIT 273-asset universe with dead coins retained (`runs/819_single_asset/POWERED_RESULT.md`, 239 live in BULL24, 267 in CHOP25), 2018-10→2026-06, TASK_899 backfill ingested. Per-asset causal features x_{i,t} (≈40): TASK_915's F1–F4 (lagged returns/trend/reversal at {1,3,7,21,63}d; Yang–Zhang σ, Parkinson/GK and YZ-to-close-to-close ratio = an intraday variance-ratio statistic, vol-of-vol, HAR terms; cross-sectional ranks, dispersion, β, idio-vol, dollar-volume rank; level-≤3 log-signature), plus CONTROLLER STATE: the forecast z-score μ̂_{i,t}/σ̂_{i,t} (TASK_915's winning cell: market-residual, vol-standardised h-day forward return), the anchor weight w_GP,i,t, the drift-adjusted current weight w̃_{i,t−1}, the cost-to-trade c·|w_GP,i,t − w̃_{i,t−1}|/σ̂_{i,t}, and a per-date context vector (cross-asset means/quantiles of the same features, DeepSets-style, so the per-asset net sees the whole book). Anchor: μ̂ from ridge, expanding window, quarterly refit, purge ≥ h; Σ̂_t = Ledoit–Wolf on trailing residual returns; aim_t = (γΣ̂_t)⁻¹ Σ_k b_k μ̂_t^{(k)} with b_k weighting slower-decaying signal families more (Gârleanu–Pedersen), decay φ_k from the measured IC autocorrelation (the loops panel's τ statistic); w_GP,t = w_GP,t−1 + (Λ⁻¹A)(aim_t − w_GP,t−1), Λ = λΣ̂ with λ calibrated so a full rebalance of gross 1 costs 21 bp-equivalent, γ set so median Σ|w| ≈ 1 with |w_i| ≤ 5% (`trader/config.py:123` per_asset_cap). Stage 1 (still closed form, decision-aware): replace the ridge coefficients by Butler–Kwon's IPO θ* = H(x)⁻¹ d(x,y) for the equality-constrained (Σw = 0, market-neutral) MVO — the linear forecast that minimises Σ̂-weighted tracking error to the ex-post optimal book rather than MSE (their Prop. 4); same features, same refit schedule, no neural net.

LEARNED RESIDUAL (Stage 2). δ_{i,t} = δ̄_{i,t} · tanh(g_θ(x_{i,t}, ctx_t)), g_θ = ONE shared MLP over per-asset features (≈40→64→64→1) plus a 64-unit context encoder, ≈15k parameters, last layer zero-initialised (Residual Policy Learning) so at initialisation w ≡ w_GP exactly. Bound δ̄_{i,t} = max(κ|w_GP,i,t|, κ_T|w_GP,i,t − w̃_{i,t−1}|), κ = 0.5, κ_T = 1: the residual may cancel or reshape a trade and re-size a bet by ≤50 %, but cannot de-lever the book. Final book w_t = Π(w_GP,t + δ_t): clip |w_i| ≤ 5 %, renormalise Σ|w_t| = Σ|w_GP,t| (gross belongs to the anchor's γ, never to θ), Σw_t = 0 if the market-neutral arm is used. Training target = the realised book itself: net_t = Σ_i w̃_{i,t−1} r_{i,t} − c·Σ_i |w_{i,t} − w̃_{i,t−1}|, c = 21 bp, turnover DRIFT-INCLUSIVE (the tactics-panel correction to `trader/backtest.py:224`, which counts target-weight changes only), |·| Huber-smoothed; loss L(θ) = −SR(net_{1:T}) + λ_δ·mean_t‖δ_t‖² + λ_θ‖θ‖², SR = mean/std·√365 over the training window (batch Sharpe as in Zhang–Zohren–Roberts; Moody–Saffell's differential Sharpe is the online variant). The gradient flows through the day-by-day simulation (a scan: δ_t changes w_t, hence next day's turnover and cost) with w_GP as a fixed input stream. Refit: expanding window from 2021-01, quarterly; each train window's last 6 months are validation ONLY for a fixed epoch budget chosen on fold 0 (excluded from the OOS aggregate — validation-Sharpe early stopping on 6 months is noise, see math); OOS = next quarter; 10 quarters 2024-Q1→2026-Q2 concatenated into one OOS series, touched once; 3 seeds (init + minibatch order); λ_δ, κ, lr, width fixed a priori on fold 0. Execution rule: rebalance at UTC close on the true daily bar to the target book, skip |Δw_i| < 0.2 % (`config.py:128`), order sizes computed on the drift-adjusted book, quantised to the ±w_unit ladder for the `eval_vector.py --operator policy-argmax --vector-weight-rebalance` second-instrument read (memo §4.3 discipline).

WHAT δ DOES MECHANICALLY. (a) Learns the multi-asset proportional-cost no-trade region: GP is a quadratic-cost solution and trades every asset every day (x_t − x_{t−1} ≠ 0 whenever aim ≠ x), which under the repo's LINEAR cost (`trader/backtest.py:188-190`, net = gross − turnover·c) is exactly the "maintenance re-trim" pattern 892 measured as value-destructive; the linear-cost optimum is a state-dependent band (Davis–Norman/Constantinides for one asset) with no closed form for 270 correlated assets. (b) Sign-preserving nonlinear shrink of the anchor's per-asset bet as a function of (μ̂/σ̂, YZ/CC ratio, cost/σ̂, current holding). (c) Cross-asset trade netting: reach the aim's factor tilt through the cheapest names. Deletion rule is part of the algorithm: δ's paired contribution vs w_GP alone is graded on the OOS series; CI including 0 ⇒ the residual is removed and the closed-form book stands or falls on TASK_915's own gates. Controlled Markov structure is not assumed anywhere: the only state δ controls is inventory, whose dynamics are known; no tree search, no learned world model.
math:
(1) Book accounting (the scorer's identity, `trader/backtest.py:188-190, 223-224`): gross_t = Σ_i w_{i,t−1} r_{i,t}; turn_t = Σ_i |w_{i,t} − w̃_{i,t−1}|; net_t = gross_t − turn_t·c, c = 21e-4; per-decision Sharpe = mean/std·√365 (`backtest.py:128-138`). Cost drag in Sharpe units = T·365·c/σ_book, T = daily turnover. 819 trend book: T = 0.155, σ_book ≈ 0.60–0.66 → 0.155·365·0.0021 = 11.9 %/yr → 0.18 Sharpe (matches POWERED_RESULT.md gross +0.74 vs net@21 +0.56). A market-neutral residual book over ~250 names has σ_book ≈ σ_idio·√ρ_resid ≈ 1.0·√(0.05–0.15) ≈ 0.22–0.39 (to be measured; central case 0.30): the SAME turnover costs 11.9 %/0.30 = 0.40 Sharpe at T = 0.155, 0.26 at T = 0.10, 0.13 at T = 0.05, 0.08 at T = 0.03. Every bp of turnover is worth ~2× more Sharpe on this book than on the trend book — the cost channel is larger here than the tactics panel's +0.10..+0.18 estimate, and it is the residual's primary source.

(2) Anchor: aim_t = (γΣ̂_t)⁻¹ Σ_k b_k μ̂^{(k)}_t; w_GP,t = w_GP,t−1 + (Λ⁻¹A)(aim_t − w_GP,t−1), Λ = λΣ̂; with Λ ∝ Σ̂ the trading matrix reduces to a scalar rate a/λ ∈ (0,1) solving a quadratic in (γ, λ, φ) (Gârleanu–Pedersen). GP turnover ≈ (a/λ)·Σ_i|aim_{i,t} − w_{i,t−1}|; with a noisy μ̂ (IC 0.03) the Markowitz aim churns ~1–2× gross per day, so T ≈ (a/λ)·(1–2) — the calibration of λ to 21 bp is what puts T in 0.03–0.15/day; measured, not assumed.

(3) Fundamental law (Grinold–Kahn; Clarke–de Silva–Thorley): gross SR ≈ IC·√BR·TC, BR = N_eff·365/h. With N_eff = 8, h = 1, TC = 0.6: gross = 32.4·IC. To clear net +0.97 at T = 0.05 (drag 0.13, σ_book 0.30) needs gross ≥ 1.10 → IC ≥ 0.034; at T = 0.10 (drag 0.26) → IC ≥ 0.038; at T = 0.155 → IC ≥ 0.042. N_eff = 15: √(5475)·0.6 = 44.4·IC → IC ≥ 0.025 (T = 0.05); N_eff = 5: 25.6·IC → IC ≥ 0.043. So the anchor needs a per-date cross-sectional IC of 0.025–0.045 at h = 1 on 2024–26, i.e. above TASK_915's G-A floor of 0.02 (G-B is where this bites). TC itself falls as trading slows (the book lags the signal), so lower T buys drag but costs TC; GP's a/λ is the closed-form balance and the residual can only shift it state-dependently.

(4) First-order value of the residual: ΔSR·σ_book ≈ 365·[E(δ_tᵀ r_{t+1}) − c·E(Δturn_t)] − SR·Δσ²_book/(2σ_book). By iterated expectations E(δ_tᵀ r_{t+1}) = E(δ_tᵀ E[r_{t+1}|F_t]): if the daily conditional mean on F_t is ≈0 the first term is ≈0 for EVERY causal δ (the loops panel's identity), leaving cost reduction (−c·ΔT, ≤ the drag numbers in (1)) and variance shaping (no expected return). Hence δ's ceiling with no forecast: +0.08..+0.40 Sharpe from turnover 0.155→0.03 on a 30 %-vol book — and only if the anchor is not flat.

(5) Detectability of the paired contribution: for two books whose daily returns differ by d_t, SE(ΔSR) ≈ (SD(d)/σ_book)/√T_yr. T_yr = 2.5 (2024-01→2026-06): a residual perturbing 40 % of book vol gives SE ≈ 0.4·0.63 = 0.25 → a true +0.15 is undetectable (needs SE ≤ 0.075, i.e. SD(d)/σ_book ≤ 0.12). A detectable residual is therefore one whose return path stays within ~12 % of the anchor's and is cheaper — the cost channel, whose paired difference is nearly deterministic. Alpha-reweighting gains of +0.1..+0.2 cannot be certified on 2.5 years.

(6) Multiplicity, SR0(N) = E[max SR_N | H0] (Bailey–López de Prado eq. 1 with E = 0): SR0 = √V·[(1−γ)Z⁻¹(1−1/N) + γZ⁻¹(1−1/(Ne))], γ = 0.5772, √V = SE of an annualised Sharpe ≈ 1/√T_yr. On the 2.5-yr window (√V = 0.63): N = 8 → +0.92, N = 20 → +1.20, N = 50 → +1.43, N = 160 → +1.70 — eight cells already produce the +0.97 bar by chance. On a 6-month validation window (√V = 1.41) with N = 5 checkpoints: SR0 = +1.69 — validation-Sharpe early stopping is noise, hence the fixed epoch budget. On the 7.7-yr PIT span (√V = 0.36): N = 160 → +0.97.

(7) Seed variance is bounded by construction: |w − w_GP| ≤ κ|w_GP| per asset with fixed gross, so the OOS seed spread cannot reproduce 875's 1.0–2.0 (which came from unanchored policies); this is a design property, not a claim about edge.
profit_source: Cost reduction, attributed to the learned part alone: a state-dependent multi-asset no-trade region under proportional (21 bp) cost, which the quadratic-cost GP anchor does not have and for which no closed form exists at 270 correlated assets. Worth at most the drag arithmetic in math (1): +0.08..+0.40 Sharpe on a 25–40 %-vol market-neutral book, ≈70–80 % of which a one-parameter hysteresis band (tactics-panel row 2) would also capture. Everything else in the stack is the ANCHOR's forecast, not the residual's: TASK_915's conditional-mean forecast of the market-residual, vol-standardised h-day forward return (y_{i,t,h} = (r_{i,t→t+h} − β̂ r_mkt)/σ̂_YZ). The IPO stage re-estimates the same forecast under a decision loss; the residual may re-weight it nonlinearly but forecasts no new quantity and creates no conditional mean. If TASK_915 reads IC ≈ 0 the anchor is ≈ flat, the residual's expected gross is 0 by iterated expectations, and the mechanism's only remaining term is a cost saving on a book that has nothing to save.
why_learning: Four pieces of information a closed-form estimator uses inefficiently or not at all, each named with its closed-form competitor: (1) The multi-asset proportional-cost no-trade region. GP (quadratic cost) trades every asset every day; Davis–Norman/Constantinides give the band for ONE asset; the 270-asset band depends jointly on (μ̂_i/σ̂_i, c/σ̂_i, Σ̂, current holdings) and has no closed form — a policy-shaped object estimable by parameter sharing across ~250 assets × ~900 days ≈ 225k decisions per refit. A one-parameter band is the closed-form competitor and must be an arm. (2) Interaction of forecast strength × range-based vol regime × cost: the GP aim is linear in μ̂ through Σ̂⁻¹; a decision loss can learn a sign-preserving nonlinear shrink where IC is state-dependent. Prior against: 819's fixed tanh sizing read −0.09 vs sign (PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md robustness) and inverse-vol −0.06 — untrained transforms on a trend signal, so weak evidence either way. (3) Cross-asset netting: reaching a factor tilt through the cheapest names is a combinatorial allocation the per-asset GP recursion does not see. (4) Decision-aware calibration of the forecast itself: Butler–Kwon show the IPO coefficients θ* = H⁻¹d minimise Σ̂-weighted tracking error to the ex-post optimal book (Prop. 4) and beat OLS most when covariance estimation error is large and SNR is low (their Figs. 4–6, res 5–10) — exactly crypto daily (SNR ≪ 1 %, 30–90-day covariance windows). This piece is CLOSED FORM: 'learning' here means a better estimator, not a network. Honest boundary: none of (1)–(4) can create a conditional mean; Elmachtoub–Grigas prove least squares is also SPO-consistent and 'performs well when the ground truth is near linear' — the decision loss buys robustness to misspecification, not signal.

bear_positive.argument: The book is market-neutral by construction of the anchor's target (β̂-residual returns, Σw = 0 arm), so it is BEAR-positive IN EXPECTATION iff the forecast carries IC in the bear; BEAR22 lies inside the training window, so it is a form check, not evidence. The residual cannot add bear positivity: with no forecast its expected gross is zero in every regime (math (4)) and it can only save cost. The only bear-positive behaviour on the record is the trend book's short leg — BEAR22 baseline +1.095 vs long-flat −2.471 (LEDGER `898/trend-decay`) — which is a forecast, not a tactic. Two unmodelled items bite exactly in bears: (i) the cost of carrying ~50 % of gross short on spot margin (borrow not modelled anywhere in `trader/`), (ii) hold-shares de-leveraging of winning shorts moved BEAR22 gross +0.225 vs +1.218 (`experiments/830_corridor/SPEC.md:95-98`) — the drift-inclusive accounting in the loss is there to price it, not to remove it.

guards: 887 ADAPTIVE HOLD: the flat state is unreachable by θ — w = Π(w_GP + δ) with Σ|w| pinned to Σ|w_GP| and |δ_i| ≤ max(κ|w_GP,i|, κ_T|Δw_GP,i|); gross is set by the anchor's γ. The collapse mode that remains is 'δ cancels every GP trade' (turnover → 0, the rational response to negative-EV trades, the 887 fixed point in a new costume); it is made visible and pre-registered as FAIL: OOS turnover < 0.01/day or > 50 % of days with zero trades ⇒ residual DELETED (the tactics panel's '>50 % flat = FAIL' rule). If the anchor itself is near-flat (IC ≈ 0 ⇒ aim ≈ 0), the 'holds positions' check (median gross ≥ 0.5, no >95 %-flat days) fails at Stage 0 and δ is never trained — the anchor is graded before the residual exists. 892 RE-TRIM DAMAGE: the loss charges c·Σ|w_t − w̃_{t−1}| on the realised path with DRIFT-INCLUSIVE turnover, so maintenance re-trims are priced in training, and δ receives w̃_{t−1} and cost-to-trade as inputs so it can learn not to trade; the pre-registered diagnostic reproduces 892's decomposition — δ's paired Δ vs the anchor reported separately on entries/exits and on maintenance re-trims — and a re-trim Δ with CI < 0 kills the residual regardless of the headline. 813 SELECTION LUCK: ONE architecture, ONE hyperparameter set fixed on fold 0 (excluded from the OOS aggregate), fixed epoch budget (no validation-Sharpe early stopping: SR0(5) on 6 months = +1.69), 3 seeds all reported, OOS 2024-01→2026-06 touched once, per-year sign required; a block-Rademacher placebo arm (δ trained on dependence-preserving sign-flipped returns) must read ≈ anchor. MULTIPLICITY: every table carries SR0(N) beside the best number with N counted honestly (arms × seeds × checkpoints); on the 2.5-yr window SR0(8) = +0.92, SR0(20) = +1.20, SR0(50) = +1.43 — the design has 4 arms × 1 config, so N ≤ 12 and the bar for 'δ beats anchor' is the paired CI, not the level. INSTRUMENT: both `trader.backtest.cell_metrics` (PIT engine) and `eval_vector` (quantised ladder) must agree within 0.1 (the 882 discipline).

why_not_falsified.receipt: LEDGER `887/collapse-confirm` (A holds 99.0 % → −2.9 %, D 91.2 % → −13.8 % at fee 0) and `885/hold-collapse-screen` (the distillation loop, not search depth, drives collapse)
why_not_falsified.argument: 887 measured a self-play policy that WAS the whole book, distilling its own visit distribution over a signal it could not see, free to choose flat. ARC's learned object cannot choose gross, is anchored to a closed-form book that carries whatever forecast exists, and is trained on realised Sharpe-after-cost, not on its own targets. The identity that predicts 887 (E[gross] = Σ E[w·E(r|F)]) predicts ARC's residual has zero expected gross without a forecast — which ARC concedes and grades as a pre-registered FAIL band rather than suffers.

why_not_falsified.receipt: LEDGER `892/action-ev`: OOS Δ(policy − matched null) −0.043..−0.056, every CI < 0; entries/exits null; the anti-edge lives in maintenance re-trims Δ −0.060/−0.062/−0.050
why_not_falsified.argument: 892's subjects were imprint/ExIt policies on a strided close-only 64-slot frame whose re-trims were never priced in training (cost0 primary). ARC prices re-trims in the loss with drift-inclusive turnover and receives 892's own decomposition as a kill diagnostic. 892 is the reason the residual's primary attributed source is cost, not alpha.

why_not_falsified.receipt: LEDGER `875/wf-generalization` (1/5 folds; OOS medians flat +0.31/+0.40/+0.41 while floors swing 15×; seed spread 1.0–2.0) and `879/rung3-distill-remeasure` (search Δ 1.602 subtractive)
why_not_falsified.argument: Those verdicts are on unanchored learned policies inside a search wrapper. ARC has no wrapper; its OOS seed spread is bounded by κ by construction (math (7)); and it is graded by paired difference against its own anchor, so the 875 shape (policy indifferent to window difficulty) would show up as Δ ≈ 0 and delete the residual rather than masquerade as edge.

why_not_falsified.receipt: Memo §1.2 A-2: the vector line received highs = lows = close and volumes = ones (`jax_encoder.py:124-134`), strided closes (`env_factory.py:417-418`); §4.7 mining pass: zero GP, statarb, Kelly/vol-targeting, signature or decision-aware code in-tree
why_not_falsified.argument: No decision-aware loss, no closed-form cost-aware controller, no IPO estimator and no range-based feature has ever been run here; ARC is composed of exactly those objects on the true-daily PIT panel, so no existing verdict measures it.

why_not_falsified.receipt: `runs/819_single_asset/POWERED_RESULT.md`: gross +0.74 vs net@21 +0.56 (0.18 cost stack, turnover 0.152/day, 60–66 %-vol book); PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md robustness: H=3d +1.35 vs +0.97 net@21 with only ~0.07 attributable to cost (n = 1)
why_not_falsified.argument: The cost channel has only been measured on a high-vol trend book; the arithmetic in math (1) says the same turnover costs ~0.40 Sharpe on a 30 %-vol market-neutral book, and the H=3d read hints that timing/turnover moves gross too. Neither has been measured on a market-neutral book — the quantity ARC's residual targets.

why_not_falsified.receipt: Tactics panel (single-reviewer): execution/turnover family 'cost reduction only, 0–2 % alone; 60–70 % it adds +0.10..+0.15 to any book'; PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md lever attribution: tanh −0.09, invvol −0.06, ensemble −0.16
why_not_falsified.argument: These are the correct priors AGAINST channels (b)/(c) and they are why ARC's odds are low. They do not falsify (a): a learned state-dependent band was never tested, the panel's +0.10..+0.15 was scaled to a 66 %-vol book, and the untrained tanh/invvol transforms were applied to a sign-trend signal, not fitted under a decision loss.

literature.ref: Elmachtoub & Grigas (2022, Mgmt Sci; arXiv 1710.08005 v5) — Smart 'Predict, then Optimize'
literature.claim: Decision loss for linear-objective downstream problems; SPO+ = convex surrogate; Fisher-consistent with the true SPO loss when the conditional cost distribution is continuous and symmetric; least squares is ALSO consistent and performs well when the ground truth is near linear; SPO+ dominates under misspecification.
literature.numbers: Def. 3: ℓ_SPO+(ĉ,c) = max_{w∈S}{cᵀw − 2ĉᵀw} + 2ĉᵀw*(c) − z*(c); Prop. 3: SPO ≤ SPO+, convex in ĉ, subgradient 2(w*(c) − w*(2ĉ−c)); portfolio experiments (Fig. 5, Markowitz with variance cap) — SPO+ 'either always close to the best approach, or dominating' with the advantage growing with polynomial degree of misspecification.

literature.ref: Butler & Kwon (2023, Quant Finance; arXiv 2102.09287 v3) — Integrating prediction in mean-variance portfolio optimization
literature.claim: IPO: regression coefficients chosen to minimise realised MVO cost through the QP; closed form for unconstrained/equality-constrained MVO; θ* minimises Σ-weighted tracking error to the ex-post optimal weights; advantage largest when covariance estimation error is high and SNR low; the gradient-through-QP variant overfits under inequality constraints.
literature.numbers: θ* = H(x)⁻¹d(x,y) (eq. 16); 24 commodity futures 1986–2020, OOS 2000–2020, walk-forward 2-yr refits, δ = 50, GROSS of trading costs: unconstrained Sharpe IPO 0.7593 vs OLS 0.3735 (Table 5), MVO cost 0.354 vs 0.679, dominance ratio 97 %/68 %; market-neutral ±12.5 % box: IPO 0.6310 vs OLS 0.3421 (Table 6), DR 60–70 %; simulated SNR 0.001–0.10, IPO gain grows as covariance resolution falls 20→10→5.

literature.ref: Zhang, Zohren & Roberts (2020, J. Financial Data Science; arXiv 2005.13665 v3) — Deep Learning for Portfolio Optimization
literature.claim: Train positions end-to-end on the batch Sharpe ratio with transaction cost C·Σ|Δ(vol-scaled w)| inside the return; long-only softmax over 4 ETFs; advantage shrinks steeply with cost.
literature.numbers: LSTM 64 units, 50-day inputs, retrain every 2 yrs, OOS 2011–Apr 2020: Sharpe 1.858 (no vol scaling, C = 1 bp), 1.962 (vol-scaled, 1 bp) vs best fixed allocation 1.579; at C = 10 bp 1.403 vs allocation-4 1.299 — the edge over annual-rebalance baselines falls from +0.38 to +0.10 between 1 and 10 bp/side, i.e. ≈ −0.03 Sharpe per bp; authors attribute it to daily turnover.

literature.ref: Silver, Allen, Tenenbaum & Kaelbling (2018; arXiv 1812.06298 v2) — Residual Policy Learning
literature.claim: π_θ(s) = π(s) + f_θ(s); zero-initialise the last layer so the initial policy equals the base controller; burn in the critic before updating the actor (β = 1.0) or performance dips early; RPL improves every base controller tested and solves tasks from-scratch RL cannot.
literature.numbers: 3×256 ReLU MLP, DDPG+HER, 5 seeds, 6 MuJoCo tasks; NoisyHook base ≈0.15 success → RPL ≈0.8 while DDPG+HER from scratch stays ≈0; ComplexHook base 0.55 → ≈0.8; PickAndPlace ~10× fewer samples than from scratch; an early dip appears when the critic is poorly initialised relative to the actor.

literature.ref: Bailey & López de Prado (2014, J. Portfolio Mgmt) — The Deflated Sharpe Ratio
literature.claim: Expected maximum Sharpe across N trials under a common null; DSR test deflates for selection and non-normality.

literature.ref: Gârleanu & Pedersen (2013, J. Finance; NBER w15205) — Dynamic Trading with Predictable Returns and Transaction Costs
literature.claim: Closed-form optimal dynamic portfolio under quadratic costs: trade partially toward an aim portfolio that overweights slower-decaying predictors; superior net returns on commodity futures vs naive benchmarks.
literature.numbers: x_t = x_{t−1} + Λ⁻¹A(aim_t − x_{t−1}); aim = weighted average of current and expected future Markowitz portfolios; no Sharpe figures retrieved (abstract only).

literature.ref: Donti, Amos & Kolter (2017, NeurIPS; arXiv 1703.04529) — Task-based End-to-end Model Learning in Stochastic Optimization
literature.claim: Differentiate the task loss through argmin via implicit differentiation of the KKT system; beats MLE two-stage and black-box policy learning on inventory, grid scheduling and battery arbitrage.
literature.numbers: No numbers retrieved beyond the qualitative ordering (abstract only); the KKT-differential system is reproduced in Butler–Kwon eq. 40.

literature.ref: Uysal, Li & Mulvey (2021; arXiv 2107.04636) — End-to-end risk budgeting portfolio optimization with neural networks
literature.claim: Implicit optimisation layer inside the network learning risk contributions; gated variant filters low-return low-vol assets.
literature.numbers: OOS 2017–2021 Sharpe: model-based end-to-end 1.16, gated 1.24 vs nominal risk parity 0.79, equal weight 0.83; transaction costs and turnover not stated in the abstract.

literature.ref: Moody & Saffell (2001, IEEE Trans. Neural Networks 12(4)) — Learning to trade via direct reinforcement
literature.claim: Recurrent reinforcement learning of positions directly on a differential Sharpe ratio with transaction costs in the reward; the online analogue of the batch Sharpe loss used here.
literature.numbers: Venue/year confirmed via Semantic Scholar metadata; abstract and result figures not retrieved this session (recall: USD/GBP half-hourly and S&P 500/T-bill monthly experiments, differential Sharpe D_t = (B_{t−1}ΔA_t − ½A_{t−1}ΔB_t)/(B_{t−1} − A²_{t−1})^{3/2}).

literature.ref: Davis & Norman (1990, Math. Oper. Res.); Constantinides (1986, J. Political Economy) — proportional transaction costs
literature.claim: Under proportional costs the optimal policy is a no-trade region (band) around the frictionless target; multi-asset bands have no closed form and are computed numerically (e.g. Muthuraman–Kumar 2006).
literature.numbers: None retrieved; not fetched this session — cited as the structural reason a quadratic-cost GP anchor leaves a learnable residual under the repo's linear cost model.

literature.ref: Lim, Zohren & Roberts (2019) Deep Momentum Networks — as read in full by the tactics-panel explorer (`lore/fable_tactics_panel_2026-09-04.md`)
literature.claim: Sharpe-loss-trained position networks on futures; published cost sensitivity puts the family far past break-even at 21 bp/side.
literature.numbers: Cost slope −0.6..−0.8 Sharpe/bp, break-even 2–3 bp/side (per the panel's reading; not re-read by me).

controllability: High, by construction and by contrast with every 828-line artifact. Every position decomposes as w = Π(w_GP + δ) with |δ_i| ≤ max(0.5|w_GP,i|, |Δw_GP,i|) and Σ|w| = Σ|w_GP|: the learned part can redistribute and cancel trades, never set leverage or go flat; switching δ off yields the closed-form book at any time (the fallback is a formula, not a checkpoint). The deployable artifact is a bill of materials — ridge/IPO coefficient vector, Σ̂ recipe (Ledoit–Wolf window), Λ⁻¹A and γ, the ≤15k-parameter δ-net with its two bounds, the 5 % cap and 0.2 % band — every item inspectable and reproducible from the SPEC; refits quarterly, parameters frozen in between. Behaviour is auditable through three logged series per day: anchor turnover, δ-induced turnover change, and the entry/exit vs re-trim split (892's decomposition), plus the fraction of days with zero trades (887's attractor as a number, with a pre-registered FAIL band). Seed variance is bounded by κ (math (7)), so a single bad seed cannot produce the −8.9..+12.7 swings the 3-seed rule was created for. Where MuZero re-enters: nowhere in this design; the only controlled state is inventory with known dynamics, and the residual IS the learned controller — the memo's Option B (search as controller) is the alternative if G-B passes and G-C fails, and ARC would be the cheaper first attempt at G-C.
compute: Prerequisite: TASK_915 (CPU, ≤2 CPU-days) must run first and pass G-A; ARC does not exist without its forecast. ARC itself: Stage 0/1 (GP + IPO closed form) = dense linear algebra on ≤270×270 matrices per day, CPU minutes per quarterly refit. Stage 2: panel ≈ 273 assets × ~2000 days (2021-01→2026-06) ≈ 550k live asset-days, ~40 features; δ-net ≈ 15k parameters; one epoch = a scan over ≤ ~1000 training days × ≤270 assets (the sequential cost term forces the scan) ≈ 10^9–10^10 FLOPs; 10 refits × 3 seeds × ~150 epochs ≈ 10^12–10^13 FLOPs → minutes to <1 hour on ONE 24 GB card, or 1–3 h CPU-JAX; peak memory < 2 GB. Placebo arm doubles it. Total under 1 GPU-hour, safe_run-wrapped on gpu-server; the workstation card suffices. The 64 GB GPUs are irrelevant to this mechanism; they would only matter for a world model, which the loops panel refuted as an alpha object. Engineering: ~3–5 days (GP solver, IPO closed form, differentiable simulator with drift-inclusive turnover, `cell_metrics` and `eval_vector` graders), kill date 14 days from SPEC commit.

kill_experiment.design: Pre-registered SPEC (sha256 recorded) with FOUR arms on the identical PIT true-daily panel, costs, window and instrument, run only after TASK_915 G-A passes and only if the Stage-0 anchor holds positions (median gross ≥ 0.5, no >95 %-flat days) on 2024-01→2026-06: A = GP anchor on ridge μ̂ (TASK_915's G-A cell); B = GP on IPO θ* (closed form); B' = B plus a ONE-parameter hysteresis band θ_band ∈ {0.5σ̂} (the closed-form competitor to the residual, fixed a priori); C = B + δ_θ residual, 3 seeds, fixed architecture/hyperparameters from fold 0 (excluded), fixed epoch budget, quarterly expanding-window refits, OOS = 10 concatenated quarters 2024-Q1→2026-Q2 touched once; C0 = δ trained on block-Rademacher sign-flipped returns (placebo, dependence-preserving). Report per arm: net@21 and net@8 per-decision Sharpe with block-bootstrap CI (block 5–21 d, 2000 resamples, seed 819), by-year (2024/2025/2026H1) and BEAR22 form check, turnover/day and its entry/exit vs re-trim split, fraction of zero-trade days, median gross, σ_book; paired ΔSR(C−B'), ΔSR(C−B), ΔSR(B−A) with bootstrap CIs on the paired daily difference series; SR0(N) with N = arms × seeds × checkpoints beside every best number.
kill_experiment.instrument: Unmodified `trader.backtest.cell_metrics` (net_series at `trader/backtest.py:188-190`, turnover at :224, amended once to drift-inclusive accounting under a pre-registered flag, both accountings printed) on the PIT 273-asset panel via `trader/data.py` true-UTC bars; second instrument `experiments/835_stage4_eval/eval_vector.py --operator policy-argmax --vector-weight-rebalance` with weights quantised to the ±w_unit ladder; the two must agree within 0.1 (882 discipline). Epoch named post-E-d with the 899 seam pinned per `LEDGER.md:28-41`.
kill_experiment.pass_fail: PASS for the residual requires ALL of: median-seed ΔSR(C − B') ≥ +0.15 with paired-bootstrap CI lo > 0 and all 3 seeds ΔSR > 0; ΔSR(C − B') on the re-trim component not < 0 with CI excluding 0; C's OOS turnover ≥ 0.01/day and ≤ 50 % zero-trade days; placebo ΔSR(C0 − B') CI includes 0; both instruments within 0.1. PASS for the STACK (the goalposts): C (or B' if the residual fails) net@21 ≥ +0.97 with CI lo > 0 on 2024-01→2026-06, positive in each of 2024/2025/2026H1, BEAR22 form check positive, median gross ≥ 0.5, 3 seeds. FAIL bands and consequences, pre-committed: residual-PASS false ⇒ δ deleted permanently, the record keeps B/B' numbers; ΔSR(B − A) CI includes 0 ⇒ IPO deleted, ridge stays; anchor fails 'holds positions' ⇒ the whole row halts at Stage 0 and reports the anchor's gross/turnover/IC triple (this is TASK_915 G-C territory, not ARC's); stack-PASS false but residual-PASS true ⇒ record the measured cost-channel Sharpe and stop — no second architecture, no hyperparameter search, no re-cut window.
kill_experiment.cost: Conditional on TASK_915 (≤2 CPU-days, already queued): ~3–5 engineer-days to write, <1 GPU-hour or ~3 CPU-hours to run all five arms with seeds, one panel read of the DB, no server training lane, 14-day kill date from SPEC commit.

honest_odds: Unconditional P(ARC clears the goalposts: net@21 ≥ +0.97 PIT on 2024–26, 3 seeds, holds positions, BEAR-positive) ≈ 3–5 %. Decomposition: P(TASK_915 G-A passes) ≈ 25 % (memo prior, unchanged by anything here) × P(G-B/anchor near the bar | G-A) ≈ 40–50 % × P(the stack clears +0.97 | anchor viable) ≈ 30–40 %. Conditional on G-A AND G-B passing: P(stack clears +0.97 PIT) ≈ 20–30 %; P(the residual adds a CERTIFIED ≥ +0.15 over the one-parameter band) ≈ 15–25 % — the detectability arithmetic (math (5)) caps this regardless of truth; P(residual adds a certified positive amount of any size over the band) ≈ 30–40 %; P(IPO beats ridge by a certified margin) ≈ 30–40 % (Butler–Kwon's +0.3..+0.4 was gross of costs on 24 futures with a strong carry/trend signal). Most likely positive outcome: the cost channel reads +0.05..+0.3 Sharpe on a low-vol market-neutral book and the band captures most of it, making δ redundant. Most likely overall outcome (≈60–70 %): TASK_915 G-A fails or the anchor is near-flat, and ARC never trains — which is the correct order of operations, not a failure of the design.
open_doubts: The whole mechanism is conditional on TASK_915 G-A; an anchor with IC ≈ 0 is near-flat (aim ∝ Σ̂⁻¹μ̂ ≈ 0), fails 'holds positions' at Stage 0, and the residual is never trained — ARC cannot rescue a missing forecast and should not be queued before 915 reports.

GP is a quadratic-cost solution applied under a linear cost model; the anchor's own turnover (0.03–0.15/day is my band, not a measurement) decides whether the cost channel is worth +0.08 or +0.40, and whether the residual has anything to cut.

Detectability: a residual that changes the return path by more than ~12 % of book vol cannot have a +0.15 Sharpe contribution certified on 2.5 years; the design therefore only certifies cost-shaped residuals — alpha-reweighting claims will be undecidable and must not be promoted on point estimates.

Design tension: pinning Σ|w| to the anchor's gross forces daily re-trims as prices drift (constant-dollar), while the residual is rewarded for not trading; the drift tolerance (0.2 % band vs a wider drift allowance) is a pre-registered constant that may dominate the measured cost saving — the tactics panel estimated uncharged drift trims at −0.03..−0.04 Sharpe on the trend book.

Borrow/funding cost on the ~50 % short leg of a market-neutral spot-margin book is modelled nowhere in `trader/` and is unrecorded for the operator's account; it bites hardest in the bears where the short leg earns, and could exceed the residual's entire cost saving.

The operator's actual Kraken tier is unrecorded (no 16 bp tier exists in the July-2026 ladder per the loops panel); every net@21 number, including this design's drag arithmetic, may be optimistic or pessimistic by several bp/side.

σ_book ≈ 0.30 for the market-neutral book is an estimate from assumed residual correlation 0.05–0.15; N_eff (TASK_825, parked) and σ_book must be measured before the IC threshold in math (3) is trusted.

Non-stationarity: 898 shows the only daily signal decayed 2021→2026; a residual fitted on 2021–23 may learn a cost/vol regime that does not persist, and quarterly re-estimation is itself a re-trim source (loops panel, continual-learning row).

The Sharpe-after-cost gradient on ~900 daily observations is noisy and non-convex; Zhang–Zohren–Roberts' success on 4 ETFs with 100 epochs is not evidence for 270 crypto assets, and Butler–Kwon found their gradient-through-QP variant overfit relative to the closed form — the closed-form IPO stage may be the only part of the 'learning' that survives.

Both `cell_metrics` (`backtest.py:221-223`, log-return gross) and the loss use per-asset log returns summed; a market-neutral long/short book's rebalancing/variance term is invisible to that scorer (tactics-panel correction #2) — second-order for arithmetic Sharpe but a known blind spot.

Literature depth is uneven: GP, Donti–Amos–Kolter and Uysal–Li–Mulvey were read at abstract level; Moody–Saffell and Davis–Norman are recall only (web-search budget exhausted this session); none of those is load-bearing for a verdict, but the GP trading-rate formula should be re-derived from the paper before implementation.
